summary: Analysis of 14 days of continuous glucose monitoring and AAPS closed-loop telemetry shows exceptional overall glycemic outcomes with 99.7% Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time-Below-Range (<70 mg/dL), a mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and a low coefficient of variation (12.9%). Basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA (5.5 h), and target settings are accurately tuned across all time segments. Automation settings (SMB, UAM, safety limits) operate safely without over-delivering insulin. Postprandial glucose returns reliably to baseline within 4 hours, with mild postprandial rises up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches managed safely by the declared e-carb strategy and UAM automation.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry contains 1,345 CGM entries across 14 days with 100% data coverage, zero gaps, and a consistent 15-minute sampling cadence. Active profile configurations and meal logs are fully specified.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality shows 100.0% coverage, 0 gaps, and max gap of 15.0 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic control is outstanding with 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL, and CV 12.9%. Transient overnight nadirs of 70-71 mg/dL occurred twice but recovered spontaneously without clinical hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary shows average_glucose=117.0, time_in_range_percent=99.7, time_below_range_percent=0.0, CV=12.9%.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal segments (0.85-1.05 U/h) maintain stable overnight and fasting glucose levels near target ranges (90-115 mg/dL) without severe drift or automated over-correction.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local shows mean local glucose between 102.3 and 107.5 mg/dL overnight (00:00-05:00).

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios (9-12 g/U), ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U), and DIA (5.5 h) effectively return glucose to baseline following weekday breakfasts and dinners. Weekend brunches show a 2-hour peak of 188 mg/dL that resolves naturally by 4 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: therapy_response_windows confirm return to baseline glucose across meal events by 240m and 360m.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB (3 min interval, 45 min max basal) and UAM (30 min max UAM basal) settings operate safely, providing effective micro-bolus adjustments during postprandial surges without causing hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings shows smb_enabled=true and uam_enabled=true with zero TBR observed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific UI activation toggles (e.g. smb_always_enabled) are null in profile telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety thresholds (max_basal_u_per_hour = 2.4 U/h, max_iob_units = 8.0 U) and Dynamic ISF (100%) provide appropriate headroom without risk of insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: raw_settings indicate max_basal_u_per_hour=2.4 and max_iob_units=8.0 against maximum scheduled basal of 1.05 U/h.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity UI switch states are null in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared prebolus timing (20 min for fast carbs, 10 min for mixed brunch) and immediate bolus splits (60-70%) effectively match meal absorption profiles.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.analysis_context meal strategies align with observed therapy response windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Nightscout treatment logs do not record explicit per-meal prebolus clock timestamps.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs (20g over 120 min) for weekend brunches prevent early hypoglycemia while allowing UAM to cover delayed absorption from higher-fat meals.
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch therapy response windows show smooth recovery to 115 mg/dL at 240m without secondary spikes.

analysis_steps.findings: Synthesized evidence indicates all core profile parameters and AAPS automation settings are well-calibrated and safe. No profile parameter adjustments are required. Optional prebolus fine-tuning for weekend brunch can be evaluated.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consolidated evidence across all 8 previous analysis stages.

strengths: Exceptional overall glycemic control with 99.7% Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL) and 0.0% Time-Below-Range (<70 mg/dL).
Extremely stable overnight and fasting glucose maintenance, reflecting accurate basal rates (0.85-1.05 U/h) and target settings (90-115 mg/dL).
Highly safe closed-loop automation performance with no evidence of insulin stacking or over-correction.
Effective meal strategy execution combining prebolus timing and targeted e-carb entries for high-fat brunch meals.
issues: Mild postprandial glucose peaks reaching up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches due to high-fat meal composition and shorter prebolus timing (10 minutes).

recommendations.title: Evaluate Prebolus Timing for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch meals currently experience 2-hour postprandial peaks near 188 mg/dL before returning to target by 4 hours. Testing a slight extension of prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes may help blunt this initial peak.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal, carb ratio, ISF, DIA, and target profile settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings maintain 99.7% Time-in-Range and 0.0% hypoglycemia over 14 days, with glucose returning reliably to target across all fasting and postprandial windows.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe 2-hour postprandial glucose peaks during weekend brunches over the next 14 days to determine whether a 5-minute prebolus extension reduces peak excursion without causing pre-meal hypoglycemia.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current prebolus timing (15-20 min) and 70-100% immediate boluses for standard fast-carbohydrate meals while utilizing SMB/UAM automation. For mixed/high-fat meals, continue applying split boluses with e-carbs (20g over 120 min) to prevent early lows and late spikes.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current meal strategies achieve excellent postprandial recovery across all meal types without causing hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Track 2-hour postprandial peaks during weekend brunch when extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Deliver bolus 20 minutes prior to meal with 70% immediate split and 0g e-carbs.
exceptions.rationale: Effectively counteracts early morning insulin resistance and coffee/bread absorption.

exceptions.suggestion: Deliver bolus 10-15 minutes prior to meal with 60% immediate split and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes (+15 min offset).
exceptions.rationale: Prevents early hypoglycemia from fat-delayed absorption while letting UAM handle late glucose surges.

implementation_steps: Review current profile and AAPS settings with your diabetes care team.
Confirm that all AAPS UI switches for SMB activation and Autosens are configured as intended.
Maintain all active profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, target) without making profile adjustments.
If desired, evaluate extending weekend brunch prebolus timing by 5 minutes while monitoring glucose closely.
education: Time-in-Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time-Below-Range indicates optimal profile tuning and highly safe closed-loop performance.
Higher-fat meals naturally delay gastric emptying, causing glucose spikes 2 to 4 hours after eating; e-carbs help AAPS anticipate this delayed absorption.
Maintaining a realistic DIA (5.5 hours) prevents the closed-loop system from stacking insulin during multi-hour postprandial periods.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support and educational review only; always independently verify all proposed therapy settings.
Consult your healthcare provider before modifying basal rates, carb ratios, or insulin sensitivity factors.
Make setting changes one at a time and monitor blood glucose closely following any adjustment.
